passages.text: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.
passages.sermon:
Cornelius lived in Caesarea.
Cornelius was a man.
Cornelius served as a centurion.
Cornelius belonged to the Italian Regiment.
The Italian Regiment was a group of soldiers.
People called this group the Italian Regiment.
passages.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ἐν Καισαρείᾳ ὀνόματι Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης ἐκ σπείρης τῆς καλουμένης Ἰταλικῆς

passages.text: He and all his household were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly.
passages.sermon:
Cornelius lived in Caesarea.
He was a centurion in the Italian Regiment.
Cornelius was devout.
He feared God.
His whole household was also devout and God-fearing.
Cornelius gave many gifts to the people.
He prayed to God all the time.
passages.original: εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν Θεὸν σὺν παντὶ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς τῷ λαῷ καὶ δεόμενος τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ παντός

passages.text: One day at about the ninth hour, he had a clear vision of an angel of God who came to him and said, “Cornelius!”
passages.sermon:
Cornelius was a centurion in Caesarea.
He was part of the Italian Regiment.
One day, at about the ninth hour, Cornelius saw a vision.
The vision was clear.
An angel of God came to Cornelius.
The angel spoke to him.
The angel said, “Cornelius!”
passages.original: εἶδεν ἐν ὁράματι φανερῶς ὡσεὶ περὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην τῆς ἡμέρας ἄγγελον τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελθόντα πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εἰπόντα αὐτῷ Κορνήλιε

passages.text: Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have ascended as a memorial offering before God.
passages.sermon:
Cornelius was a devout and God-fearing man.
He saw an angel of God in a vision.
Cornelius stared at the angel.
He became afraid.
Cornelius asked, "What is it, Lord?"
The angel answered him.
The angel said, "Your prayers have come up before God."
The angel said, "Your gifts to the poor have come up before God."
The angel said, "God remembers your prayers and your gifts."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἔμφοβος γενόμενος εἶπεν Τί ἐστιν Κύριε Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Αἱ προσευχαί σου καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἀνέβησαν εἰς μνημόσυνον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter.
passages.sermon:
The angel spoke to Cornelius.
The angel gave Cornelius a command.
The angel told Cornelius to send men to Joppa.
The angel told Cornelius to call for a man named Simon.
This Simon is also called Peter.
passages.original: καὶ νῦν πέμψον ἄνδρας εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνά τινα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος

passages.text: He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter is staying with a man named Simon.
Simon is a tanner.
Simon the tanner lives in a house.
His house is by the sea.
passages.original: οὗτος ξενίζεται παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ ᾧ ἐστιν οἰκία παρὰ θάλασσαν

passages.text: When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants.
passages.sermon:
Cornelius was a Roman centurion.
An angel spoke to Cornelius.
The angel left Cornelius.
Cornelius called two of his servants.
Cornelius also called a devout soldier.
This soldier was one of his attendants.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν αὐτῷ φωνήσας δύο τῶν οἰκετῶν καὶ στρατιώτην εὐσεβῆ τῶν προσκαρτερούντων αὐτῷ

passages.text: He explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa.
passages.sermon:
Cornelius was a Roman centurion.
Cornelius had seen an angel.
Cornelius called two of his servants.
Cornelius also called a devout soldier who served him.
Cornelius explained everything that had happened to them.
Cornelius sent them to Joppa.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξηγησάμενος ἅπαντα αὐτοῖς ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Ἰόππην

passages.text: The next day at about the sixth hour, as the men were approaching the city on their journey, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
The next day, some men traveled toward the city.
These men were approaching the city.
At about the sixth hour, Peter went up on the roof.
Peter went up to pray.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ὁδοιπορούντων ἐκείνων καὶ τῇ πόλει ἐγγιζόντων ἀνέβη Πέτρος ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα προσεύξασθαι περὶ ὥραν ἕκτην

passages.text: He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
passages.sermon:
Peter was on the roof.
Peter became hungry.
Peter wanted to eat something.
Other people were preparing a meal.
While they prepared the meal, Peter fell into a trance.
passages.original: ἐγένετο δὲ πρόσπεινος καὶ ἤθελεν γεύσασθαι παρασκευαζόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐγένετο ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔκστασις

passages.text: He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
passages.sermon:
Peter was on the roof.
Peter was praying.
Peter saw heaven open.
Peter saw something coming down from heaven.
It looked like a large sheet.
The sheet was being let down to earth.
The sheet hung by its four corners.
passages.original: καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγμένον καὶ καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιέμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: It contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air.
passages.sermon:
The sheet held many animals.
It held all kinds of four-footed animals.
It held reptiles that live on the earth.
It held birds that fly in the sky.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ ὑπῆρχεν πάντα τὰ τετράποδα καὶ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς καὶ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!”
passages.sermon:
Peter saw a vision from God.
Peter saw heaven open.
Peter saw a large sheet come down to earth.
The sheet held many animals.
A voice spoke to Peter.
The voice said, “Get up, Peter.
Kill and eat.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀναστάς Πέτρε θῦσον καὶ φάγε

passages.text: “No, Lord!” Peter answered. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to the Lord.
Peter said, “No, Lord.”
Peter explained his actions.
Peter said, “I have never eaten anything impure.”
Peter said, “I have never eaten anything unclean.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν Μηδαμῶς Κύριε ὅτι οὐδέποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ἀκάθαρτον

passages.text: The voice spoke to him a second time: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Peter in a vision.
\r\nGod used a voice to speak.
\r\nThe voice spoke to Peter a second time.
\r\nThe voice gave a command.
\r\nThe voice said, “Do not call anything impure.”
\r\nGod has made these things clean.
\r\nDo not call what God has made clean impure.
passages.original: Καὶ φωνὴ πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου πρὸς αὐτόν Ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου

passages.text: This happened three times, and all at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
passages.sermon:
God gave Peter a vision.
God repeated the vision three times.
A sheet appeared in the vision.
God took the sheet up into heaven immediately after the third time.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνελήμφθη τὸ σκεῦος εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν

passages.text: While Peter was puzzling over the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and approached the gate.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter saw a vision.
Peter did not understand the vision.
Peter wondered about the meaning of the vision.
Cornelius was a Roman centurion.
Cornelius sent men to find Peter.
The men searched for Simon’s house.
Simon was also called Peter.
The men found Simon’s house.
The men came to the gate of the house.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ διηπόρει ὁ Πέτρος τί ἂν εἴη τὸ ὅραμα ὃ εἶδεν ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Κορνηλίου διερωτήσαντες τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ Σίμωνος ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸν πυλῶνα

passages.text: They called out to ask if Simon called Peter was staying there.
passages.sermon:
The men stood at the gate of Simon’s house.
They called out.
They asked a question.
They wanted to know if Simon, who is also called Peter, was staying there.
passages.original: καὶ φωνήσαντες ἐπυνθάνοντο εἰ Σίμων ὁ ἐπικαλούμενος Πέτρος ἐνθάδε ξενίζεται

passages.text: As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.
passages.sermon:
Peter was thinking about the vision.
Peter did not understand the vision’s meaning.
The Holy Spirit spoke to Peter.
The Holy Spirit said, “Three men are looking for you.”
passages.original: Τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ὁράματος εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες τρεῖς ζητοῦντές σε

passages.text: So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit spoke to Peter.
The Spirit said, “Get up.
Go downstairs.
Go with these men.
Do not hesitate.
I have sent them.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς

passages.text: So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter went down to the men.
Peter spoke to the men.
Peter said, “I am the one you are looking for.”
Peter asked, “Why have you come?”
passages.original: Καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι ὃν ζητεῖτε τίς ἡ αἰτία δι’ ἣν πάρεστε

passages.text: “Cornelius the centurion has sent us,” they said. “He is a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you.”
passages.sermon:
Cornelius is a centurion.
He sent us.
Cornelius is a righteous man.
He fears God.
All the Jewish people speak well of him.
A holy angel spoke to Cornelius.
The angel told him to send for you.
The angel said you should come to his house.
Cornelius wants to hear a message from you.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν Θεὸν μαρτυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ ὅλου τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου ἁγίου μεταπέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥήματα παρὰ σοῦ

passages.text: So Peter invited them in as his guests. And the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter invited the men into his house.
He treated them as his guests.
The next day, Peter got up.
He left the house with the men.
Some of the brothers from Joppa went with Peter.
passages.original: Εἰσκαλεσάμενος οὖν αὐτοὺς ἐξένισεν Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς καί τινες τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἀπὸ Ἰόππης συνῆλθον αὐτῷ

passages.text: The following day he arrived in Caesarea, where Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
passages.sermon:
Peter traveled to Caesarea the next day.
Cornelius lived in Caesarea.
Cornelius was waiting for Peter and his companions.
Cornelius had gathered his relatives.
Cornelius had also gathered his close friends.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν ὁ δὲ Κορνήλιος ἦν προσδοκῶν αὐτοὺς συνκαλεσάμενος τοὺς συγγενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἀναγκαίους φίλους

passages.text: As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.
passages.sermon:
Peter was about to enter the house.
Cornelius met Peter at the entrance.
Cornelius fell at Peter’s feet.
Cornelius tried to worship Peter.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν τὸν Πέτρον συναντήσας αὐτῷ ὁ Κορνήλιος πεσὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας προσεκύνησεν

passages.text: But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Cornelius fell at Peter’s feet.
Peter helped Cornelius get up.
Peter said, “Stand up.”
Peter said, “I am only a man.”
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων Ἀνάστηθι καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὸς ἄνθρωπός εἰμι

passages.text: As Peter talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter spoke with Cornelius.
Peter went inside the house.
Peter saw many people gathered together.
passages.original: Καὶ συνομιλῶν αὐτῷ εἰσῆλθεν καὶ εὑρίσκει συνεληλυθότας πολλούς

passages.text: He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a Jew.
Peter spoke to the people gathered in the house.
Peter said, “You know it is against our law for a Jew to associate with a foreigner.
You know it is against our law for a Jew to visit a foreigner.
But God has shown me something new.
God has shown me that I should not call any person impure.
God has shown me that I should not call any person unclean.”
passages.original: ἔφη τε πρὸς αὐτούς Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὡς ἀθέμιτόν ἐστιν ἀνδρὶ Ἰουδαίῳ κολλᾶσθαι ἢ προσέρχεσθαι ἀλλοφύλῳ κἀμοὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἔδειξεν μηδένα κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον λέγειν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a Jew and an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter spoke to the people gathered in the house.
Peter said, “You invited me to come here.
I came right away.
I did not object.
Now I ask you a question.
Why did you send for me?”
passages.original: διὸ καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως ἦλθον μεταπεμφθείς πυνθάνομαι οὖν Τίνι λόγῳ μετεπέμψασθέ με

passages.text: Cornelius answered: “Four days ago I was in my house praying at this, the ninth hour. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God.
passages.sermon:
Cornelius was a Roman centurion.
Cornelius spoke to Peter.
He said, “Four days ago, I was in my house.
It was the ninth hour of the day.
I was praying.
Suddenly, a man stood in front of me.
He wore bright, shining clothes.
He said to me, ‘Cornelius, God has heard your prayer.
God has remembered your gifts to the poor.’”
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος ἔφη Ἀπὸ τετάρτης ἡμέρας μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ὥρας ἤμην τὴν ἐνάτην προσευχόμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἔστη ἐνώπιόν μου ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ καὶ φησίν Κορνήλιε εἰσηκούσθη σου ἡ προσευχὴ καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἐμνήσθησαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Cornelius in a vision.
God told Cornelius to send men to Joppa.
God told Cornelius to find Simon, who is also called Peter.
Peter is staying as a guest in the house of Simon the tanner.
Simon the tanner’s house is by the sea.
passages.original: πέμψον οὖν εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετακάλεσαι Σίμωνα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος οὗτος ξενίζεται ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος βυρσέως παρὰ θάλασσαν

passages.text: So I sent for you immediately, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.”
passages.sermon:
Cornelius was a Roman centurion who feared God and gave generously to the poor.
Cornelius said, “I sent for you right away.
You came here willingly.
Now we are all gathered here before God.
We are ready to listen to everything the Lord has commanded you to say.”
passages.original: Ἐξαυτῆς οὖν ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ σύ τε καλῶς ἐποίησας παραγενόμενος νῦν οὖν πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ πάρεσμεν ἀκοῦσαι πάντα τὰ προστεταγμένα σοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism, but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter began to speak.
Peter said, “I now truly understand something about God.
God does not show favoritism.
God accepts people from every nation.
God welcomes anyone who fears Him.
God welcomes anyone who does what is right.”
passages.original: Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν Ἐπ’ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ Θεός ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν

passages.text: He has sent this message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the gospel of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
passages.sermon:
God sent a message to the people of Israel.
This message announces good news.
The good news is about peace.
God gives this peace through Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is Lord of all people.
passages.original: τὸν λόγον ὃν ἀπέστειλεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ οὗτός ἐστιν πάντων Κύριος

passages.text: You yourselves know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee with the baptism that John proclaimed: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
passages.sermon:
You know what happened throughout Judea.
These events began in Galilee.
They started after John preached baptism.
God anointed Jesus of Nazareth.
God gave Jesus the Holy Spirit and power.
Jesus went everywhere doing good.
Jesus healed all who were oppressed by the devil.
God was with Jesus.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς οἴδατε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐκήρυξεν Ἰωάννης Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: We are witnesses of all that He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. And although they put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree, God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen— not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
passages.sermon:
We are witnesses of everything Jesus did.
He did these things in the land of the Jews.
He also did them in Jerusalem.
They killed Jesus.
They hung Him on a tree.
God raised Jesus on the third day.
God made Jesus appear to people.
Not everyone saw Him.
Only the witnesses chosen by God saw Him.
We are those witnesses.
We ate with Jesus after He rose from the dead.
We drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
passages.original: Καὶ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου τοῦτον ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀλλὰ μάρτυσιν τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῖν οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.
passages.sermon:
Jesus commanded us.
He told us to preach to the people.
He told us to testify about Him.
God appointed Jesus.
God chose Jesus to be the Judge.
Jesus will judge the living.
Jesus will judge the dead.
passages.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ Κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν

passages.text: All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”
passages.sermon:
All the prophets speak about Jesus.
They say something important about Him.
They say that God forgives sins through Jesus’ name.
Every person who believes in Jesus receives this forgiveness.
passages.original: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.
passages.sermon:
Peter was speaking to the people.
He was telling them about Jesus Christ.
All the people listened to Peter’s message.
The Holy Spirit came down on everyone who heard the message.
passages.original: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον

passages.text: All the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.
passages.sermon:
The circumcised believers had come with Peter.
These believers saw what happened.
They were astounded.
They saw that God gave the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles.
God poured out the gift of the Holy Spirit on the Gentiles.
This surprised the circumcised believers.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἐκκέχυται

passages.text: For they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God. Then Peter said, “Can anyone withhold the water to baptize these people? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was with a group of believers.
These believers saw the Holy Spirit come upon Gentiles.
They heard the Gentiles speak in tongues.
They heard the Gentiles praise God.
Peter responded to this event.
Peter said, “No one can withhold water for baptism from these people.”
Peter explained why.
He said, “They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.”
passages.original: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν Θεόν Τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ δύναται κωλῦσαί τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἔλαβον ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς

passages.text: So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.
passages.sermon:
Peter was the leader of the apostles.
Peter saw that the Gentiles had received the Holy Spirit.
Peter gave a command.
He ordered them to be baptized.
He said they must be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
After this, the Gentiles spoke to Peter.
They asked Peter to stay with them.
They wanted him to remain for a few days.
passages.original: προσέταξεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς
